target_customer: iPhone and iPad Touch owners who stream Hulu and Netflix on a computer
problem: Hulu and Netflix ran in the browser, so Apple's Remote and most remote apps could not control them. teevoxRemote let a phone act as a remote with one-touch show selection, synced viewing with a friend and play, pause and volume control.
product_category: Mobile remote control for web video

founders.name: Jong-Moon Kim (Jiggity)
founders.background_notes: YC page lists Jiggity Kim; TechCrunch 2010-08-19 gives the full name and spells the first name Jung in metadata.

founders.name: Andrew Sugaya
founders.background_notes: Named by TechCrunch (2010-08-19) as a co-founder; not on the YC page.

competitors.name: PlayOn
competitors.what: Let users watch Netflix and Hulu on their phones

competitors.name: Apple Remote
competitors.what: Apple's app controlling iTunes movies, not browser video

technical_complexity.rationale: Relaying commands through a server to a browser session was a modest engineering task, with the added need to track Hulu and Netflix page changes.

defensibility.rationale: The trick depended on controlling third party web players and was copyable in weeks, and the streaming services could ship their own remotes.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: A BetaNews article found in search says Hulu later released an official remote app for iOS and Android; its date was not opened, so the timing is unverified.

market_need_then: Streaming from a laptop to a TV was growing in 2010 and TechCrunch noted the lack of existing apps that could control Hulu and Netflix in the browser without extra hardware.

branding.domain_note: teevox.com is still held; the fetch returned a page titled Warp Prism, details unclear.
branding.community_and_virality: Launch coverage in TechCrunch, AppAdvice and Geeky Gadgets in August 2010, but no evidence of a lasting community.

brand_strength.rationale: Only short launch-week coverage found; trademark search shows similar names (Televox, Tekvox) which suggests confusability.

outcome_analysis: Teevox launched teevoxRemote in August 2010 to TechCrunch coverage and raised only a small seed, with YC listing it inactive. No post-mortem or acquisition was found, so the cause of inactivity is not public and no failure factors are asserted. The product relied on controlling Hulu and Netflix in the browser, which left it exposed to the services' own remote apps.
notes: The $20K seed rests on a single database (CB Insights), dated 2010-06-26, and is probably the YC deal; the same page conflicts by calling the company alive. Dealroom lists Teevox as closed. The teevox.com fetch returned only a title 'Warp Prism' and is unreliable. Founder education is 'former MIT students' per TechCrunch only. The Hulu official remote claim is from a search snippet, not opened.
